opening: The sandstorm had buried half the relay chain and scattered the expedition’s route markers across a basin of red dunes. When the emergency beacons began repeating fragments of one broken distress call, the five-person team brought every surviving trace into the field shelter: pairing sheets, clock records, route sketches, sequence logs, and sealed token photographs. Several names seemed persuasive for ordinary human reasons. The review board rejected those impressions and required one reconstruction under the expedition’s own rules.

scenes.prose:
Before anyone argued over the fragments, the panel read the governing notice beside the shelter door. For this incident, the board had declared the coherent signal bearer protocol active; ordinary rank and reputation did not count. The reviewers then fixed one shared status scale for the entire inquiry: clear counted as 0, dormant as 1, stable as 2, waking as 3, latent as 4, and open as 5.

A slate beside the notice described the local tally procedure. It began at 6 and, in order, took the relation, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol statuses, using coefficients 11, 13, 5, 3, 2, and 7. At each stream, the panel squared the current tally, added that stream’s coefficient multiplied by its status value, and kept the remainder modulo 97. The calculation made three passes: first in the stated order, then in reverse order with the coefficients reversed, and then once more in the stated order with the coefficient list rotated one place to the left. Without resetting the tally, the panel repeated that complete three-pass cycle 115 times.
scenes.title: The Rule at the Shelter Door

scenes.prose:
The first crate yielded the pairing sheet. Its legible carbon copy put Sawyer Okada’s team pairing at stable, while a torn edge of the roster still marked Casey Rossi’s team pairing as dormant. The two entries were clipped together because the auditors were checking whether the storm had separated a planned relay pair.

A clock-backed beacon entry placed Morgan Okada’s signal interval at stable. Nearby, the repeater trace that followed Drew Nguyen registered as clear; the trace was checked because its timing determined whether the fragment belonged to the same emergency call. Causal review gave Gray Meier’s repeater response an open status after analysts followed the failure mark through the damaged relay strip.

At the northern access hatch, door and route checks placed Sawyer Okada’s beacon sector at stable. Witnesses standing in the corridor put Casey Rossi’s beacon sector at clear. The reconstruction ledger kept Morgan Okada’s relay order at latent, and a close photograph of the recovered token set marked Drew Nguyen’s cipher glyph latent. At the final inventory check, Gray Meier’s cipher glyph remained stable.
scenes.title: Pairings, Doors, and Tokens

scenes.prose:
The next bundle had survived inside a sealed map tube. A witness who checked the roster left Drew Nguyen’s team pairing at waking, while clerks wrote latent beside Gray Meier’s team pairing on the sealed worksheet. The panel kept both entries because the witness had seen the roster before the sandstorm, whereas the worksheet had been closed during the evacuation.

Clocked entries put Sawyer Okada’s signal interval at dormant. The sequence sheet, checked against the beacon’s internal clock, showed Casey Rossi’s signal interval as waking. Downstream checks tied Morgan Okada to a latent repeater response, a useful comparison because the response was recorded one pylon beyond the first failure.

A movement sketch marked Drew Nguyen’s beacon sector as latent, and the route ledger tied Gray Meier’s beacon sector to dormant. In the ordered log, Sawyer Okada’s relay order appeared as waking; the ordered sheet showed Casey Rossi’s relay order as clear. Finally, inventory counted Morgan Okada’s cipher glyph as dormant.
scenes.title: The Sealed Worksheet

scenes.prose:
The oldest pairing note, recovered beneath a warped instrument case, gave Morgan Okada’s team pairing an open status. The timesheet review then left Drew Nguyen’s signal interval open, while reconciled timing notes kept Gray Meier’s signal interval at latent; the reviewers compared those records because the same burst appeared to cross two damaged clocks.

Instruments tracing Sawyer Okada’s action left the repeater response dormant. When Casey Rossi acted, the repeater response came back waking, a result preserved with the failure trace rather than inferred from anyone’s account. Location review left Morgan Okada’s beacon sector waking.

The remaining marks concerned order and transmission method. Sequence notes placed Drew Nguyen’s relay order at dormant, while sequence review kept Gray Meier’s relay order stable. Token and seal checks left Sawyer Okada’s cipher glyph clear. The sealed check showed Casey Rossi’s cipher glyph waking.
scenes.title: Timing, Movement, and Seals

scenes.prose:
With every fragment assigned to its evidence stream, the panel ran the prescribed passes without resetting the tally between them. For this incident, the accepted tally was 58.

The final definition was strict: the coherent signal bearer was the one person whose six-stream tally equaled the accepted tally. No rank, reputation, conspicuous action, or narrative prominence could substitute for that calculation. The reviewers sealed the reconstructed incident record and left the names to be tested by the checksum.
scenes.title: The Accepted Record

title: Coherent Signal Bearer — Case 10000
